args.body: Take the existing CATALOGUE-AGENCY-SUBCONTRACT-INTAKE mission under a valid lease. Start with a first-party e-commerce implementation or product-information agency supplier intake. Use the mission's existing two-page limit and exclude previously screened prospects. Verify whether the agency pays subcontractors for discrete catalogue or export QA, who can apply, and whether the published route permits an operator response. A partner badge, sales referral form or job application alone does not meet those conditions. For a qualifying agency, map a quoted requirement to the actual clean-control and duplicate-image output in products/services/catalogue-text-fulfillment/clean-and-duplicate-run.json, or run one fictional case if that requirement is untested. Save the source passage and hash, observed acceptance evidence and one copy-ready operator response with AI disclosure. Record standing intake separately from a current purchase request. If neither page qualifies, save the exclusions and the exact evidence that would reopen the route. Read back the committed result before closing with a lesson. No external submission, account creation, agreement, spending or deployment.

description: Commercial feedback is available as unverified interpretations. The snapshot shows zero classified signals and five unclassified sources, so demand remains unknown. Use it to test whether an agency explicitly buys this work and offers a usable supplier response route. The separate item 4 pilot depends on an authorized operator's send-or-decline decision. A redacted send receipt would establish exposure, and an eligible inbound inquiry can advance independently. Public deployment remains subject to host-enforced independent review.
